items.title: CVE-2026-103603 (HIGH 8.7): Memory allocation with excessive size value in the HSS/LMS signature code (HssPublicKeyParameters, HssSignatu…
items.one_liner: Bouncy Castle's C# library is vulnerable to a memory exhaustion DoS attack via maliciously crafted HSS/LMS signatures.
items.summary: A high-severity denial-of-service vulnerability exists in the Legion of the Bouncy Castle bc-csharp library (versions before 2.7.0) within its HSS/LMS signature verification code. An unauthenticated remote attacker can supply a specially crafted HSS public key with an excessive level count, causing the library to allocate massive amounts of memory during signature parsing. This can lead to an OutOfMemoryException or consume up to 17 GB of memory per verification attempt. Developers using this library for cryptographic operations should upgrade to version 2.7.0 or later.
key_facts: Impact: Denial of Service via memory exhaustion
items.bottom_line: Applications relying on Bouncy Castle for HSS/LMS signature verification are susceptible to remote memory exhaustion attacks and must be updated to prevent service disruption.

items.title: LLM Anonymization Against Agentic Re-Identification
items.one_liner: AURA provides a new LLM-based anonymization method that balances privacy against re-identification by agentic web-search tools while retaining data utility.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced AURA (Anonymization with Utility-Retention Adaptation), an LLM-powered framework designed to protect text from re-identification by agentic LLMs with web search capabilities. The framework uses a mask-reconstruct approach that separates privacy localization from utility-preserving reconstruction, selecting candidates based on adversarial checks. Evaluations show that AURA achieves lower re-identification counts compared to other non-differential privacy methods while maintaining higher contextual utility. This addresses the growing threat where weak contextual cues in text can be cross-referenced via web-search agents.
items.bottom_line: AURA offers a practical defense for developers handling sensitive text that may be processed by agentic LLMs, effectively reducing the risk of re-identification via web-search cross-referencing.

items.title: The Agent Said It Was Done. The Database Disagreed.
items.one_liner: A new benchmark from Microsoft and Hugging Face shows that nearly 78% of failed agent trials still report clean tool execution while leaving incorrect database states behind.
items.summary: Microsoft and Hugging Face researchers introduced ThinkingBox, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents by grading their terminal backend state and side effects rather than just looking at final responses or tool calls. In a common-set ablation of 121,680 trials across 12 LLM models, researchers found that 79,853 attempts failed executable backend checks, with 67.24% of those failures still terminating cleanly without a reported tool error. Among those failures, executable checks identified wrong field values in 77.61%, unintended extra effects in 43.30%, and missing required effects in 25.36%. The findings demonstrate a massive gap where AI agents can appear successful while leaving incorrect records behind in databases.
items.bottom_line: AI agents frequently report successful tool execution while leaving underlying database records in an incorrect state, requiring backend-state verification rather than proxy metrics.
